Figure 1:OverSeer sees beyond what agents see.Two agents interact in a shared Minecraft environment (Left).
In addition to generating each agent’s egocentric view (Bottom), OverSeer  models six fixed-pose auxiliary cameras (Right).
These auxiliary streams establish a persistent shared reference, enforcing world consistency over time and agent consistency across views.

Figure 2:OverSeer design overview.Aδ\delta-VAE (Left) compresses each fixed auxiliary stream into compact residual codes relative to its first-frame reference, and OverSeer (Right) jointly generates agent latents and these residual codes, conditioned on T5-encoded actions via cross-attention and Plücker-ray camera poses via AdaLN.

Figure 3:OverSeer keeps the agents consistent across views.Generated videos inMinecraft,GZDoomand a multi-cameraReal Capture, each at two moments (before, after). Each agent’s trail is one
3D track projected into every auxiliary camera (Agent 1 blue, Agent 2 orange); it lands on the
generated agent in each of them, so the agents are consistent across views.

Figure 4:δ\delta-VAE residual codes carry the movers, not the scene.Four cross-scene
transfers: a host anchor is decoded with a donor clip’s residual code (transfer, purple band) instead of
its own (control), at two moments (before, after). The donor’s mover (white box) appears in the host
scene (purple box) while the host scene itself is preserved.

Figure 5:OverSeer keeps the world consistent over time.On the three revisiting tasks
(reunite at start, reunite far, dynamic event), OverSeer shows the partner and the crater where the
ground truth does, while Solaris andγ\gamma-World mostly do not.

Figure 8:Additional MAC-Bench results in Minecraft.Top: the three benchmark
tasks. Bottom: three further dynamic events. OverSeer recovers the partner or the evolved
event state where the ground truth does, while the egocentric-only variant does not.

Figure 9:MAC-Bench results in Doom.Reunite tasks on three Freedoom maps.
OverSeer restores the partner after the agents separate; the egocentric-only variant does
not.

Figure 10:Long rollouts in Minecraft.Each block shows both agent views and all
six auxiliary views over3030s.

Figure 11:Long rollouts in Doom.Each block shows both agent views and all eight
auxiliary views over2121s.

Figure 12:Long rollouts on real-world multi-camera captures.Left: both agent
views and all six auxiliary views over3030s. Right: top-down layout of the auxiliary
cameras and agent trajectories.
